title: Connecting, failures and loading
note: One screen on the opaque night backdrop for the join (its steps and each failure in plain words), a session that ended (lost, map failed, error), a host that could not start, and the map loading with the players and a tip or a how-to card. Leaving (left, closed) shows nothing here: straight back to the ship (the game boots into the ship; the suit menu, s5, joins and hosts). Every text is rebuilt on NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED. Open (the engineer's design): whether loading shows the aliens' flight to Earth (m8 §1). The how-to card holds as many frames as its task needs and scrolls sideways when they do not fit (the engineer, 2026-10-22); its art is a placeholder here (below).

states.label: Пошук
states.note: A code join, step FINDING; the host's name is not known yet. CONNECTING looks the same with connect.step.connecting.

states.label: Напряму
states.note: A Direct join (LAN or VPN): it starts at CONNECTING, shows no code row and no address.

states.label: Вхід
states.note: Step JOINED; the host's lobby name has arrived (#214).

states.label: Версія
states.note: wrong_version, wrong_content, service_refused, unknown_map; the two version lines when known.

states.label: Втрачено
states.note: host_lost: a running session ended (from the lobby or a round).

states.label: Не створено
states.note: cannot_host: Host (with a code or directly) could not start.

states.label: Завантаження
states.note: From the Loading phase until pre game (s6): this machine's progress, the players, one random tip.

states.label: З карткою
states.note: As load, with the how-to card of a task type in this round the player has not completed instead of the players and the tip.

nodes.name: Night
nodes.note: Opaque; the style's darkest, used as the decided black. mouse_filter STOP, so nothing behind it takes input.

nodes.name: Connecting
nodes.note: Shown from Join until the lobby (s4) or a failure, as one quiet tile (the target page's tile language): the step in small capitals over the title, the time since Join at the right; at the foot, a code join shows the code, a Direct join shows no address and no code.

children.name: Spinner
children.note: Turns once a second about its centre (pivot_offset_ratio 0.5, 0.5); half speed under reduced motion.

children.name: Step
children.note: JoinProgress.step(): FINDING -> connect.step.finding, CONNECTING -> connect.step.connecting, JOINED -> connect.step.joined. A Direct join starts at CONNECTING. The tile's head; the game sets uppercase = true.

children.name: Title
children.note: connect.connecting_unnamed until the host's lobby name arrives (#214), then connect.connecting with {lobby}: a name the host typed is player data and never translated; while the host's lobby name is the default, {lobby} = tr("lobby.default_name") with the host's name, as on s4.

children.name: Elapsed
children.note: The time since Join as m:ss, updated every second (auto_translate_mode DISABLED).

children.name: CodeRow
children.note: A code join only (hidden for a Direct join).

children.name: Text
children.note: The code typed in the suit menu (s5 ship-code; auto_translate_mode DISABLED).

children.name: Space
children.note: Pushes Cancel to the right edge.

children.name: Cancel
children.note: The only button, so ToyButtonSecondary, as the failure's lone Back. It takes focus on open with the ring hidden: grab_focus(true) (Control.grab_focus's hide_focus, Godot 4.5+; unconfirmed for 4.7.2), so the ring shows only after an arrow or d-pad press. Esc (ui_cancel) does the same. Aborts the join and returns to the ship with the suit menu open where the join started (s5 ship-code or ship-direct), the code or address kept in its field. The traversal timeout is the game's (M6 §2.3).

nodes.name: Failure
nodes.note: One quiet tile for every failure: what happened, then one action and Back at the left. The texts come from the EndReasons id (the table in the spec, s3).

children.name: Title
children.note: Join failures share connect.fail.title; a session that ended or a host that could not start has its own title.

children.name: Versions
children.note: fail-version only, and only when the game can name the versions (protocol and content from JoinProgress.found_detail); hidden when unknown.

children.name: Primary
children.note: connect.fail.retry tries the same target again (host-failed: hosts again the same way); connect.fail.direct returns to the ship with the suit menu open on Join by address (s5 ship-direct). Absent where the failure has no action. It takes focus on open with the ring hidden (grab_focus(true), as Connecting/Cancel).

children.name: BackGhost
children.note: Back beside Primary (a ghost button): returns to the ship with the suit menu open on Game (s5 ship); after a join failure the code or address stays in its field. Esc does the same.

children.name: BackSolo
children.note: Back when it is the only button (no_room, the version failures, lost, map failed, error): ToyButtonSecondary. Same action as BackGhost; the two are separate nodes because their variations differ. It takes focus on open with the ring hidden (grab_focus(true), as Connecting/Cancel).

nodes.name: Loading
nodes.note: One quiet tile in the middle: the title over this machine's progress, then the players under their own small-capitals head. Whether loading shows the aliens' flight to Earth (the lobby is their spaceship) is open: m8 §1.

children.name: Bar
children.note: This machine's load fraction.

children.name: Players
children.note: One row per player, the host first, then in join order; the own row (Row) reads player.you, the other rows the player's name (auto_translate_mode DISABLED).

children.name: Head
children.note: The players' head (the lobby's word); the game sets uppercase = true.

children.name: HostRow
children.note: A hairline row (the target's settings rows): the name at the left, the state at the right.

children.name: State
children.note: loading.player_loading in ToySettingRowValue (dim) while the player loads; loading.player_ready in ToySettingRowText once loaded.

nodes.name: Tip
nodes.note: One quiet line in its own tile at the bottom centre, hugging the text.

children.name: Text
children.note: One random tip.* key per loading (tip.neighbours, tip.two_hands).

nodes.name: Head
nodes.note: As Loading's top, a quiet tile over the card: the title over the progress. As wide as the card (its 1384 px of frames and its margins).

nodes.name: Card
nodes.note: The how-to card (P8) of a task type in this round that the player has not completed: at most twice per type and never after its first completion (user:// counters, #254). Content data per task type; here Cooking, one of the MVP's five, with PLACEHOLDER art (see Frames). No line says the task is new. A card has as many frames as its task needs (Cooking has seven, 352 px art each); the card shows three and a half of them and its frames scroll sideways inside it (Scroll).

children.name: Head
children.note: The card's head as a tile head: howto.label in small capitals over the task's name.

children.name: Note
children.note: The game sets uppercase = true.

children.name: Scroll
children.note: The frames scroll sideways when they do not fit (the engineer, 2026-10-22): a card holds as many frames as its task needs. No bar is drawn (SCROLL_MODE_SHOW_NEVER) until the pack has a sideways bar; the frame cut at the card's edge shows there is more. The wheel scrolls it sideways while vertical scrolling is disabled, a drag on a touch screen too (unconfirmed for Godot 4.7.2: check ScrollContainer's wheel handling); follow_focus true. The view shows three and a half frames (1384 px), so the cut frame says the card goes on.

children.name: Art
children.note: PLACEHOLDER art: seven own-work Delivery frames (dist/pack/cards/delivery-meaning-1..3, delivery-1..3 and delivery-meaning-4, 640x480, transparent) stand in for the Cooking card's seven frames, which the engineer named every card's placeholder (2026-10-22). Those frames are generated art kept in the art track (prime-game-art#272) and this repo's licence list does not cover generated art yet, so the game takes them from the art track's pack. expand_mode IGNORE_352x264 here and in s8, 272x204 in s5's Guide, stretch_mode KEEP_ASPECT_CENTERED; SIZE here; the same card in s3, s5 and s8. The cards are wordless: a frame holds only its art, no caption.

children.name: Frame7
children.note: The frame that shows the finish.
